newsitem.title: USA: Physician Sales drops on Q4 forecast.
newsitem.headline: Physician Sales drops on Q4 forecast.

text.p: Shares of Physician Sales & Service Inc dropped about 32 percent in early trading Monday after the medical supplies distributor said it expects to post a fourth quarter loss due to acquisition-related charges, despite higher revenues.
Physician Sales lost 4-1/2 to 9-1/2 and was one of the most active Nasdaq issues.

The Jacksonville, Fla.-based company expects to post a loss of $0.05 to $0.07 a share for the fourth quarter ended March 28 compared with a profit of $0.12 a share last year. On a consensus basis, analysts expected Physician Sales to earn $0.15 a share in the fourth quarter, according to First Call.
Physician Sales said its expected loss will include several acquisition-related charges which come to a total of $0.19 to $0.24 a share.
The company said fourth quarter revenues should rise 30 percent to about $187 million from last year. For the year, revenues should also increase 30 percent to $690 million.
Physician Sales said it believes that the anticipated earnings decline is due to one-time, non-recurring events.
Physician Sales also said it changed its method of reserving and escrowing for the realization of assets acquired for its most recent acquisitions.
Analysts said the change in accounting methodology will help the company in the long-term but will not produce an immediate benefit.

"It's an aggressively-run company in a volatile business. It will continue to be at the center of controversy and the stock will continue to be volatile," said Michael LeConey, an analyst with National Securities Corp.
"To date, these periods of (the stock price) being beaten up have been buying opportunities. It could turn out to be that way again," LeConey said.
